strings.name: Barry Barish
strings.role: Experimental physicist · Organizer of large scientific projects
strings.summary: Barish trained in physics at UC Berkeley and spent much of his career at Caltech, initially studying particles and neutrinos. From 1994 he led LIGO construction and organization, developing collaboration and detector implementation. The collaboration first directly detected gravitational waves in 2015. He shared the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics with Weiss and Thorne and later joined Stony Brook University.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped build and organize the large LIGO scientific project, advancing gravitational-wave detection from research proposals to observational results.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Omaha, Nebraska, United States; born in 1936.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Building LIGO
strings.highlights.h1.text: Organized detector construction and international collaboration, turning a longstanding research plan into operating observatories.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BA (1957) and physics PhD (1962), University of California, Berkeley.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Shared Nobel Prize
strings.highlights.h2.text: Shared the 2017 physics prize with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne; gravitational-wave observations were the collaboration’s achievement.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joined Stony Brook
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined Stony Brook University in the autumn as an endowed professor of physics.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t2.text: Three scientists were honored for decisive contributions to the LIGO detector and gravitational-wave observation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: First gravitational-wave signal
strings.timeline.t3.text: LIGO detected a signal from merging black holes; the team announced the result the following year.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Led linear collider design
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became director of the International Linear Collider Global Design Effort, serving until 2012.
strings.timeline.t5.title: LIGO director
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became LIGO director and helped establish the LIGO Scientific Collaboration.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Took charge of LIGO construction
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became principal investigator and reorganized construction and management plans.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Caltech
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joined as a research fellow and continued experimental high-energy physics.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Physics doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed his doctorate at Berkeley after earning his bachelor’s degree in 1957.
